language-modes.note: site/app.js applyLanguage() (line 539) switches document.lang and preview copy between English, Cantonese and bilingual, wired from initSettings() language-mode select. This is a real, wired switch but only changes one preview string, not the whole site's rendered copy - most page text has no data-copy hook.

funny-levels.note: site/app.js initSettings() wires english-funny and cantonese-funny selects to state.englishFunny/state.cantoneseFunny (line 895), and applyCopy() (line 654) plus copyText()/copyLevel() (lines 640-653) genuinely restyle rendered text: the COPY table (lines 546-644) holds eight keys (heroLede, themeDesc, motionDesc, emptyDestinations, emptyNotifications, notifSettingSaved, notifSettingsReset, notifRegexApplied), each with four real English and four real Cantonese variants indexed by the chosen level, and changing a select re-runs applyCopy() and visibly changes the rendered string. The real gap is coverage, not mechanism: only three elements (site/index.html, site/settings.html) carry a data-copy hook (heroLede, themeDesc, motionDesc) and the other five COPY keys are notification strings - eight styled strings total out of the whole site's copy, with everything else fixed at one tone. The selects also only offer four levels (0-3, defaulting to 0/Plain) rather than the canonical five levels defaulting to 5/Maximum.

regex-builder.note: site/app.js implements a real anchored regex builder: openRegex()/initRegex() (lines 808, 812) open a <dialog> attached to the triggering field (regex-target-label shows "Attached to: <field>"), support literal-insert buttons, i/m/u flags, and previewRegex() live matching, with applyRegex() writing the result back into the originating search field. Wired from every .regex-trigger button via initSearch() (line 807), including the settings search and documentation search.

non-blocking-notifications.note: site/app.js implements notify()/notification history (renderNotifications, notification-history dialog) with bulk select/dismiss (initNotificationBulk, planBulk with destructive flag), a notification-open dialog, and export of notification history (notificationExportRows). Wired end to end from init() (line 1055).

material-appearance.note: site/app.js implements a genuine infinite-colour-picker/translator (rgbToHsl/hsvToRgb/rgbToLab/rgbToOklab/hwbToRgb/cmykToRgb and translateColour, wired via initColourTranslator) plus theme/density/accent/font-scale controls in initSettings() with a live preview (initSettingsPreview). This covers colour translation and basic tokens well, but there is no per-element "Edit appearance..." editor, no Word-depth typography controls, and no named-preset export/import beyond the general settings export.

app-logo-customization.note: site/app.js wires logo-file/logo-clear to loadLogo()/applyLogo() with a logo-status readout, storing the custom logo in localStorage. No such converter surface exists.

command-palette.note: site/app.js implements openPalette() (line 816) opening a real <dialog id="command-palette"> with a live-filtered palette-search field and renderPalette() (line 815), wired both from a palette-open button and from Ctrl+Shift+F: initNavigation() (line 777) attaches a document-level keydown listener that checks event.ctrlKey&&event.shiftKey&&event.key.toLowerCase()==='f', calls preventDefault, and invokes openPalette() directly - the chord is genuinely wired everywhere the listener is attached (every page). partial is still the correct label, for a different reason: renderPalette() (line 815) only indexes six static pages (Home/Product/Documentation/Downloads/Status/Settings) and the DESTINATIONS documentation catalogue - it never indexes settings controls, so a person cannot reach an individual setting through the palette the way the console app's palette reaches an individual control.

destructive-action-confirmation.note: site/app.js planBulk() and bulk actions carry a destructive flag (line 299, 309) that changes copy to state "This cannot be undone," and settings-reset is styled as a danger-button, but no two-key-plus-slider super-confirmation gate (the documented contract's specific mechanism) was found - only a plain destructive-labelled action.

local-version-history.note: The documentation catalogue lists a "History" article (app/history, describing append-only local configuration revisions) as PRODUCT documentation content, but no actual history/versions panel, diff view, or restore action exists in the site itself - this is a described feature of the console product, not an implemented feature of the site.

complete-exports.note: site/app.js implements a genuinely broad export pipeline: toJson/toJsonl/toYaml/toToml/toXml/toSql/toDelimited/toMarkdown/toHtml plus suitableFormats()/exportFilename()/download(), used by both initDocumentationExport() and the settings/notification export paths, with an explicit personalVocabulary:"omitted" marker in the settings export payload (line ~895) matching the export-honesty contract.

bulk-actions.note: site/app.js implements planBulk()/summariseBulk()/bulkClick()/bulkSelectAll() with a reviewable affected/skipped preview and a destructive flag, wired into notification bulk-select/dismiss (initNotificationBulk).

accessibility.note: site/app.js implements a real WCAG contrast calculator (contrastRatio/contrastVerdict, lines 519-520) used by the colour translator, and sr-only labels appear in settings.html (4 occurrences), but no site-wide audit of focus order or ARIA roles was performed. reduceMotion() (line 930) itself is checked at five call sites, not one: initReveals() (line 780, scroll-triggered reveal animations), the number-counter animate() count-up (line 967), and initConnectionDiagram()'s start() gate plus its own guard immediately after (lines 996 and 999, the animated data-path indicator) - every animated surface on the site consults it, and it also composes the OS prefers-reduced-motion query with the site's own low-motion setting rather than only one of the two.

responsive-sizing.note: site/styles.css implements a real, systematic responsive strategy: body{min-width:320px} (line 98), 32 separate clamp() uses for fluid type and spacing, and 13 @media rules covering five breakpoints (1100px, 900px, 720px, 640px, 520px) that collapse the primary nav into a hamburger menu, reflow grids to single columns, and restack the settings/download/status layouts. site/app.js's initNavigation() (line 774) wires a real nav-toggle button that opens/closes the collapsed #site-nav menu and manages aria-expanded, matching the CSS breakpoint. Not marked implemented because no JS-level narrow-width state flag (comparable to the app's "narrow" screen flag) drives any layout decision, and the responsive behaviour has not been captured/verified at 100/125/150/200% display scale.

personal-vocabulary-upload.note: site/app.js wires vocabulary-file/vocabulary-clear to loadVocabulary()/applyVocabulary(), with bounded validation of replacement entries (from/to length limits, line ~924) and a vocabulary-status readout, storing the cache in localStorage under ding-pbx-vocabulary-cache.

browser-extension-download-surfaces.note: This is a static documentation/marketing site; there is no browser extension and no Start-download/Downloading/complete dialog surfaces.

offline-documentation-browser.note: site/documentation.html plus renderDestinations()/initDocumentationExport() in site/app.js present a searchable documentation catalogue with per-article export. The DESTINATIONS catalogue (site/app.js line 4) is a plain array literal embedded directly in app.js, not fetched separately at runtime - app.js contains zero fetch() calls, so there is no network request for the catalogue beyond the ordinary one-time load of the page's own script. The real gap is that each result links out to a separate static article page (docs/${item.article}.html) rather than rendering parsed article content in place the way the console app's docs-markdown.ts renders headings/paragraphs/links in-app; this site has no in-page markdown-to-block renderer.

bounded-overlays.note: The regex builder (openRegex) and command palette (openPalette) both use native <dialog>.showModal(), which the browser bounds to the viewport and paints its own surface, and openRegex() explicitly labels which field it is attached to ("Attached to: <field>"). This satisfies the bounded/anchored-overlay contract for these two surfaces.
